statement_record.book: Rough Definition: a symmetric monoidal structure on a category C is a unit object I and a functor ⊗ : C × C → C together with natural isomorphisms λ_c : I ⊗ c ≅ c, ρ_c : c ⊗ I ≅ c, α : (c⊗d)⊗e ≅ c⊗(d⊗e) and a swap σ_{c,d} : c⊗d ≅ d⊗c with σ∘σ = id, all required only to be 'well behaved' (the coherence axioms are deliberately suppressed).
statement_record.intree: Class Monoidal (I, tensor : C ∏ C ⟶ C, unit_left, unit_right, tensor_assoc, six naturality squares, triangle_identity, pentagon_identity) + Class BraidedMonoidal (braid, braid_natural, both hexagons) + Class SymmetricMonoidal (braid_invol : braid ∘ braid ≈ id[x ⨂ y]).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the book explicitly suppresses the coherence axioms ('rough'), while the in-tree classes impose them in full — triangle and pentagon for the monoidal part, both hexagons for the braiding, plus the naturality squares in to- and from-form. The book's σ is an isomorphism outright; in-tree braid is a bare morphism made invertible by braid_invol, which is equivalent. Setoid rephrasing (≈ on hom-setoids) throughout.

statement_record.book: Let (C, I, ⊗) be symmetric monoidal and c an object. A dual for c is (i) an object c*, (ii) η_c : I → c* ⊗ c, (iii) ε_c : c ⊗ c* → I, satisfying the two snake equations (4.59): c ≅ c⊗I → c⊗(c*⊗c) ≅ (c⊗c*)⊗c → I⊗c ≅ c equals id_c, and symmetrically for c*. If every object has a dual, C is compact closed.

statement_record.book: If C is compact closed then (1) C is monoidal closed: for all c,d there is an object c ⊸ d with C(b ⊗ c, d) ≅ C(b, c ⊸ d) natural in b (take c ⊸ d := c* ⊗ d, precomposing with id_b ⊗ η_c); (2) any two duals c* and c' of c are isomorphic; (3) c ≅ c**.
statement_record.intree: Clause (2) is available in bicategorical form: adjoint_unique says two right adjoints of the same 1-cell are isomorphic, and since the delooping Monoidal_OneObject_Bicategory makes bicat tt tt definitionally C with hcompose = tensor and the BicatAdjunction triangles literally the snake equations, a dual of c is exactly a right adjoint of c and adjoint_unique yields c* ≅ c'. Clauses (1) and (3) have no in-tree counterpart over CompactClosed.

For (3): the double-dual isomorphism appears in-tree only as star_double_dual, a FIELD of Class StarAutonomous over a different (dualizing-object, internal-hom) notion of dual — assumed, not proved, and not about compact closure.
